name: Learn LLVM 17: hand-written lexer and recursive-descent parser (tinylang)
listed_description: Book techniques: hand-written lexer and recursive-descent parser (tinylang); the book cites compilation speed as the reason many compilers, clang among them, use a handwritten lexer.
reason: Code present (Chapter03/tinylang/lib/Lexer/Lexer.cpp, 200 lines; lib/Parser/Parser.cpp, 693 lines; same lexer in Chapter04) but no numeric comparison against flex, bison or any other baseline anywhere reachable. Repo has no benchmark folder or timing code (grep of the lexer, parser, codegen, TableGen and CMake files for benchmark, faster, speed, perform, time finds nothing); README is the Packt boilerplate (MIT, 224 stars, 5 commits, code imported 2023-12-27, later commits only README banners); the issues page shows 0 results. Directional claim only.

name: Learn LLVM 17: Braun et al. SSA construction with phi simplification
listed_description: Book techniques: Braun et al. SSA construction with phi simplification (readLocalVariable, sealed blocks, optimizePhi); the book says it runs very fast even without the phi optimization.
reason: Code present (Chapter04/tinylang/lib/CodeGen/CGProcedure.cpp, 445 lines: readLocalVariableRecursive, addEmptyPhi, addPhiOperands, optimizePhi) but no timing, no benchmark code and no named baseline in the repo (no mem2reg or load/store comparison numbers); no issues; no linked benchmark repo. Directional claim only.

name: Learn LLVM 17: TableGen-generated token filter (tinylang keyword lookup)
listed_description: Book techniques: TableGen-generated token filter for tinylang keyword lookup; the book says a plain binary search does not beat llvm::StringMap and a generated perfect hash is needed to beat it.
reason: Repo Chapter08/TableGen/TokenEmitter.cpp (230 lines) emits a sorted table with std::lower_bound (binary search) plus an optional SELFCHECK correctness test; it does not carry a perfect-hash emitter, no benchmark harness, and no timings. The only qualitative claim is itself a negative result for the code that is present (binary search does not beat llvm::StringMap). No numbers against llvm::StringMap anywhere reachable (repo files, 0 issues, one web search on the topic found nothing).
